name: Carolina Precision Switchgear
old_description: Carolina Precision Switchgear specializes in refurbishing low and medium voltage circuit breakers restoring the equipment back to pristine condition.
about:
Carolina Precision Switchgear operates from Concord, North Carolina, in the Charlotte metropolitan area. The company was founded in 2006 by Doug Weaver, a former U.S. Navy interior communications specialist who spent 24 years as a nuclear supervisor at Duke Energy performing power-factor testing and circuit-breaker repair. Weaver launched the business to provide specialized refurbishing and testing services for low- and medium-voltage switchgear.

The firm’s core work is restoring circuit breakers to original performance through a full disassembly, cleaning, plating (silver or dichromate), repair, and reassembly process carried out by Level II PEARL‑certified technicians. A 10,000‑square‑foot facility houses calibrated test equipment including primary‑injection sets, while mobile trailers bring the same capabilities to customer sites. Through its affiliation with Group CBS, the company also offers engineering support, training, and access to over 800 CBS ArcSafe remote‑racking and remote‑switching products.

Customers span utilities, manufacturing plants, and commercial facilities. The shop services equipment from major manufacturers such as ABB, GE, Westinghouse/Eaton, Siemens, Square D, and Federal Pacific, as well as obsolete brands. Services range from preventive maintenance and infrared thermography to arc‑flash studies, high‑current testing, cable VLF/tan‑delta testing, and emergency troubleshooting.

The company emphasizes that reconditioning existing breakers can cost roughly 30 % of a new retrofill installation, saving customers tens of thousands of dollars. Its differentiation rests on the combination of in‑shop and on‑site capabilities, PEARL‑certified personnel, and the parts inventory and remote‑operation tools supplied by the Group CBS network.
